command.name: schema
command.summary: Describe every command this build contains
command.description:
Prints the command surface as data: flags with types and enums, required inputs, whether a command mutates or destroys, its output kind, and the exit codes it can produce.
With no argument it lists every command. With a dotted command name it prints that one command in full. It is generated from the same registry that builds the command tree, so it cannot drift from what the binary actually does — and it lists only what this build contains.

flag.name: limit
flag.usage: maximum results, or "all" to exhaust the result set

global-flag.name: format
global-flag.usage: output format: tsv|xml|json|yaml (default: tsv for lists, xml for records). JIRA_FORMAT sets it for every command

global-flag.name: describe
global-flag.usage: print this command's schema instead of running it

global-flag.name: context
global-flag.usage: use this context for one invocation, without selecting it

global-flag.name: api-version
global-flag.usage: force the REST version, 2 or 3, and skip the deployment probe

global-flag.name: ca-bundle
global-flag.usage: PEM file of certificates to trust in addition to the system roots

global-flag.name: readonly
global-flag.usage: refuse any command that would change Jira

global-flag.name: debug
global-flag.usage: trace HTTP requests to stderr; credentials are redacted in the transport

global-flag.name: refresh
global-flag.usage: ignore cached site metadata and probe again

global-flag.name: retries
global-flag.usage: retry budget per request; exhausting it exits 8 or 9, never 0

global-flag.name: max-requests
global-flag.usage: cap total HTTP calls for this invocation; 0 means no cap

exit-codes.exit-code: Bad flags, missing required input, unsupported combination
Succeeded but result set was truncated

command.example: jr schema jr schema version jr schema --format json
